_note: Every myth/domain reference in Pantheon Wars points at one of these ids. G/N/E sources were opened and read on 2026-10-29 while building v0.1. Sources M/I/X/H/Y/J/V were added for v0.2 on 2026-10-29; direct page fetches were blocked by the build environment network policy, so each claim was checked against the search-index summary of the cited page (field verification). Game mechanics are original abstractions; they are not claims about historical or present-day worship practice.

G1.title: ZEUS - Greek God of the Sky, King of the Gods
G1.supports: Zeus as god of sky, weather, law and order, oaths; thunderbolt attribute; Dodona oak oracle where priests were inspired by rustling oak leaves; source of prophetic signs (panomphaios).

G2.title: ATHENA (Athene) - Greek Goddess of Wisdom, War & Crafts
G2.supports: Athena as goddess of wisdom and good counsel, war, the defence of towns, heroic endeavour, weaving, pottery and crafts.

G3.title: DEMETER - Greek Goddess of Grain & Agriculture
G3.supports: Demeter as goddess of agriculture, grain and bread who sustained mankind with the earth's bounty.

G4.title: POSEIDON - Greek God of the Sea & Earthquakes
G4.supports: Poseidon as god of the sea, rivers, floods and drought, earthquakes and horses.

G5.title: Hesiod, Theogony (trans. Evelyn-White)
G5.supports: Genealogy of the Olympians; Cyclopes arm Zeus with thunder and lightning; Prometheus.

G6.title: Homeric Hymns (incl. Hymn 2 To Demeter, trans. Evelyn-White)
G6.supports: Hymn to Demeter: Demeter's grief withholding and restoring the grain harvest.

N1.title: Odin | Myth & History
N1.supports: Odin as war god, protector of heroes, great magician associated with runes, god of poets; the wolf and the raven dedicated to him; gave an eye for wisdom.

N2.title: Thor | Germanic God, Norse Mythology, Thunder, & Hammer
N2.supports: Thor's name is the Germanic word for thunder; the hammer Mjollnir represents the thunderbolt and returns to the thrower; foe of giants but benevolent toward humankind; widely worshipped in Iceland.

N3.title: Freyr | God of Fertility, Harvest & Peace
N3.supports: Freyr as ruler of peace and fertility, rain and sunshine; of the Vanir; the boar sacred to him.

N4.title: Norn | Norse gods, fate, destiny
N4.supports: Norns as maidens who spun or wove the fate of men (Urd, Verdandi, Skuld), living by Yggdrasill under Urd's well.

N5.title: Hovamol (Havamal), The Poetic Edda, trans. Henry Adams Bellows (1936)
N5.supports: Stanzas 138-146: Othin hangs on the windy tree (Yggdrasil) and takes up the runes; stanza 142: 'Each word led me on to another word'; runes and charms (Ljothatal).

N6.title: Voluspo (Voluspa), The Poetic Edda, trans. Henry Adams Bellows (1936)
N6.supports: Stanzas 19-20: the ash Yggdrasil green by Urth's well; the three maidens Urth, Verthandi and Skuld scored the wood, made laws and set the fates of men.

E1.title: Re | God, Egypt, Sun
E1.supports: Re as sun god and creator who travels across the sky in his solar bark and through the underworld by night, vanquishing the serpent Apopis; father of Maat; centre of worship at Heliopolis.

E2.title: Maat | Truth, Justice, Balance
E2.supports: Maat as personification of truth, justice and cosmic order; weighing of the heart against Maat's feather; maat (order) set in place of isfet (disorder).

E3.title: Osiris | Description, Myth, Symbols, & Facts
E3.supports: Osiris as god of fertility and ruler of the dead who granted all life from the underworld, from sprouting vegetation to the annual flood of the Nile; 'Osiris garden' of Nile-moistened soil sown with grain.

E4.title: Thoth | God, Symbol, & Facts
E4.supports: Thoth as god of the moon, reckoning, learning and writing; scribe and adviser of the gods; ibis and baboon sacred to him.

E5.title: Isis | Description, Myth, Symbols, History, & Facts (J. Tyldesley)
E5.supports: Isis's name is the Greek form of the Egyptian word for 'throne'; magical healer and protector; still revered by pagans today.

E6.title: The Egyptian Book of the Dead, trans. E. A. Wallis Budge (1895)
E6.supports: Primary-text context for funerary religion, judgment of the dead and solar hymns.

M1.title: Enlil/Ellil (god)
M1.publisher: Ancient Mesopotamian Gods and Goddesses (Oracc / UK Higher Education Academy)
M1.supports: Enlil decreed the fates, his command could not be altered, and he granted kingship; main sanctuary the Ekur at Nippur. The 'Lord Wind' reading of the name is a contested, apparently secondary interpretation.
M1.verification: search-index summary of this exact URL reviewed; page not opened directly (network policy)

M2.title: Enki/Ea (god)
M2.supports: Enki/Ea as god of wisdom, magic and incantations residing in the subterranean fresh-water ocean (abzu); patron of arts and crafts; associated with Eridu and the E-abzu temple. The Akkadian name Ea is attested from the 24th century BCE; when he merged with Enki is unclear.
M2.verification: search-index summary of this exact URL reviewed; page not opened directly (network policy)

M3.title: Inana/Ištar (goddess)
M3.supports: Inana/Ištar's astral aspect as the planet Venus (morning and evening star); the eight-pointed star as her most common symbol; the rosette also used in later periods.
M3.verification: search-index summary of this exact URL reviewed; page not opened directly (network policy)

M4.title: Utu/Šamaš (god)
M4.supports: Utu/Šamaš as sun god associated with justice and divination; at sunrise he emerges and takes a daily path across the sky, seeing what happens below.
M4.verification: search-index summary of this exact URL reviewed; page not opened directly (network policy)

M5.title: Apkallu (Iconography of Deities and Demons, electronic pre-publication)
M5.publisher: University of Zurich, Department of Religious Studies
M5.supports: The seven apkallu sages associated with Enki/Ea and Eridu, credited with bringing civilising knowledge; apotropaic figurines.
M5.verification: search-index summary of this exact URL reviewed; page not opened directly (network policy)

M6.title: Ziggurat of Ur (Art History I, Lumen Learning / SUNY)
M6.supports: The Ur ziggurat (c. 2100 BCE, Ur-Nammu) dedicated to Nanna: mud-brick core, baked-brick casing, three monumental stairways rising to terraces with a temple on top (summit shrine lost).

I2.title: Cath Maige Tuired §168 (CELT edition)

I3.title: Lugh (Cath Maige Tuired episode at Tara)
I3.supports: Lugh Samildánach ('equally skilled in many arts') admitted to Tara after showing he holds every skill at once; made chief ollam.

I4.title: The Dagda
I4.publisher: Wikipedia (secondary summary of medieval Irish sources)
I4.supports: The Dagda associated with abundance; his cauldron (one of the four treasures of the Tuatha Dé Danann) from which no company went away unsatisfied (Lebor Gabála / Cath Maige Tuired tradition).

I5.supports: Cormac's Glossary (c. 9th–10th c.) calls Brigit a goddess venerated by poets, with two sisters associated with healing and smithcraft, daughters of the Dagda.

I6.title: Hill of Tara

X4.title: Chalchiuhtlicue: Stone kneeling figure
X4.supports: Chalchiuhtlicue, 'she of the jade skirt', goddess of lakes, streams and running water used to irrigate fields; greenstone identified with life-giving water.
